chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, there are women with us, so should I depart with them at night?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, you intend to do as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did.' I said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Depart with them at night, and do not depart with them until you pause with them at Jam', then depart with them until you bring them to the Great Jamarah, so they should pelt the Jamarah. If there is no slaughter upon them, let them take from their hair and shorten their nails, and proceed to Mecca facing it, and perform Tawaf by the House, and perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then let them return to the House and perform a week's Tawaf, then let them return to Mina, and they will have completed their Hajj.'
And he said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Usamah with them.'

key_terms.جَمْعٍ: A place near Muzdalifah where pilgrims pause
key_terms.يَسْعَيْنَ: Perform Sa'i (walking) between Safa and Marwa

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual steps for women during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual sequence for women during the Farewell Tawaf and Sa'i, emphasizing the Prophet’s precedent of sending Usamah ibn Zayd to accompany them for safety and modesty. It clarifies that while women may depart Muzdalifa at night like men, they must complete the stoning of the Jamarah al-Aqabah and the minor pilgrimage rites before returning to Mina, highlighting the practical accommodations for female pilgrims in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Saeed Al A’araj who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! There are women with us, so can they be departed with at night?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes. You are intending that you do just as Rasool-Allahsaww did’. I said, ‘Yes’. So heasws said: ‘Depart with them at night, and do not depart with them until you pause with them at Jam’a. Do not depart with them until you go with them to Al-Jamarahah al-Uzma (bigger Jamarah), so they would pelt the Jamarah. So if they do not happen to have a slaughter (of an animal) upon them, so let them take from their hair, and shorten from their nails, and they should go to Makkah in their direction, and they should do Touaf by the House (Kabah), and they should perform Sa’ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then they should return to the House, and they should perform Tawaaf of seven circuits. Then they should return to Mina, and they would have been free from their Hajj’.
And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Send Asama with them (women)’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Sa‘id al-A’raj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, there are women with us: if we can leave with them during the night. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, do you want to do just as the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, had done?’ I replied, ‘Yes, that is what we want to do.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You can leave with them during the night. You must stay along with them in Jam‘, then leave to al-Jamarah al-‘Uzma’ to throw pebbles. If they do not have to slaughter any offering, they must do Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on), then proceed to Makkah forward to perform Tawaf around the House and Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah. They then must return back to the House to perform seven times Tawaf, then return to Mina’ and their al-Hajj is complete.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, sent ‘Usamah with them (the women).”’
